project.name: simsh
project.goal: Evolve simsh into a lightweight agent runtime kernel with a trustworthy default workspace and realistic adapter-side non-core layers, using alternating implementation, review, and design-refinement loops until the repository reaches a high-confidence complete state.

features.title: Close HTTP execute or session metadata edge cases and request parsing gaps
features.description: Execution row from manual-default (manual-20260324-http-meta-request-edge-hardening). Why now: The HTTP integration surface still sits at 71.1% coverage, and code inspection shows `decodeOptionalJSON`, `describePathMeta`, and path extraction around `include_meta` are only partially exercised even though higher-level harnesses depend on them.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/service/httpapi ./pkg/service` passes with new tests for empty or null session POST bodies, invalid JSON bodies, metadata fallback or defaulting branches, and shell tokenization edge cases.

An explicit `include_meta` request that names `/` or other quoted or escaped absolute paths keeps the intended path in `meta.paths`, so metadata extraction matches the command the caller actually sent.
Coverage for `pkg/service/httpapi` improves from the current 71.1% while preserving existing success-path and session-lifecycle behavior.
risks: Keep the handler thin; prefer small parsing or metadata fixes over pushing runtime semantics into HTTP-only code.
If root-path metadata is intentionally excluded, document and test that contract explicitly instead of leaving code and comments contradictory.
features.why_now: The HTTP integration surface still sits at 71.1% coverage, and code inspection shows `decodeOptionalJSON`, `describePathMeta`, and path extraction around `include_meta` are only partially exercised even though higher-level harnesses depend on them.

features.title: Make long-run preflight resilient to transient temp-space failures
features.description: Execution row from manual-default (manual-20260324-long-run-temp-space-preflight). Why now: The current long-run loop can misclassify actionable work as blocked when temporary-file creation fails transiently, and this repo is currently operating with less than 200 MiB free on `/System/Volumes/Data`, which makes that noise recurring rather than hypothetical.
acceptance_criteria: `bash .bagakit/long-run/check_and_resume.sh` surfaces low-space or temp-file failures as a retryable preflight outcome with a deterministic hint instead of only a raw shell failure.
A rerun after a successful tiny-write sanity check keeps `next-action.json` and `feature-list.json` consistent instead of leaving the loop in a spurious no-next-action state.
`bash .bagakit/long-run/ralphloop.sh preflight --json` or equivalent runner guidance documents the exact retry path for temp-space anomalies.
risks: Keep the runner orchestration-only; do not bury project-specific repair logic inside long-run scripts.
If temp-space failures are actually durable, the new preflight must still stop the loop clearly instead of silently masking the problem.
features.why_now: The current long-run loop can misclassify actionable work as blocked when temporary-file creation fails transiently, and this repo is currently operating with less than 200 MiB free on `/System/Volumes/Data`, which makes that noise recurring rather than hypothetical.
updates: 2026-03-24T10:59:10Z synced from bk-execution-table
evidence: `make lint`, `make check`, and several package-local test runs in this session all failed at least once with `no space left on device` before succeeding again after cache cleanup or retry.

`docs/.bagakit/inbox/howto-long-run-preflight-rerun.md` already records a concrete initializer incident where a second `check_and_resume.sh` run selected the same row cleanly after a transient temp-file failure.
The generated `check_and_resume.sh` currently runs validation directly and stops on the first shell failure without classifying low-space issues as retryable loop noise.

features.title: Harden session-manager lifecycle and adapter failure edges
features.description: Execution row from manual-default (manual-20260324-session-manager-adapter-failure-edges). Why now: Session lifecycle is a core kernel contract, and `pkg/engine/runtime` still leaves the lowest coverage in `Execute` and `Resume` precisely where policy narrowing, adapter phases, and closed-session recovery interact.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime ./pkg/adapter/reference` passes with new tests for create, checkpoint, resume, or close adapter failures, blank or missing session ids, and runtime rebuild behavior after adapter-managed mounts change.
Tests prove adapter-phase failures do not partially rewrite session snapshot or checkpoint state, and closed or missing sessions keep returning stable typed errors.
Coverage for `pkg/engine/runtime` improves from the current 87.1% with direct exercise of the current low branches in `Execute`, `Resume`, and `invokeAdapterPhase`.
risks: The remaining uncovered `Execute` branches are mostly lock-loss or runtime-construction fault paths that need contrived injection rather than more lifecycle contract expansion.
Future adapters can still fail runtime reconstruction by returning invalid mounts; this pass preserves prior state on failure but does not add a broader mount-validation layer.
features.why_now: Session lifecycle is a core kernel contract, and `pkg/engine/runtime` still leaves the lowest coverage in `Execute` and `Resume` precisely where policy narrowing, adapter phases, and closed-session recovery interact.
updates: 2026-03-24T10:59:10Z synced from bk-execution-table
evidence: `pkg/engine/runtime/session_manager_test.go` now covers blank-id and blank-command handling, create/checkpoint/close/resume adapter failures, active-session resume no-op behavior, and read-only runtime rebuilds that keep adapter-projected `/memory` mounts available after failure.
`pkg/engine/runtime/runtime_core_additional_test.go` now rejects blank adapter IDs and unsupported adapter phases directly, lifting `applySessionAdapters` and `invokeAdapterPhase` coverage to 100.0%.

`pkg/engine/runtime/session_manager.go` now stages adapter mount updates until adapter hooks and any runtime rebuild both succeed, so observe/checkpoint/close failures no longer clear stored adapter mounts on the way out.

`go test ./pkg/engine/runtime -run 'TestSessionManager|TestApplySessionAdapters|TestInvokeAdapterPhase'`, `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime ./pkg/adapter/reference`, and `go test ./pkg/engine/runtime -cover` all exit 0, and runtime coverage rises from 87.1% to 93.8%.
